topics.label: Course introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the cancer biology lecture series, the student cohort, and the primary learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as genetic disruption of tissue differentiation and architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how accumulated genetic and epigenetic alterations cause cells to fail their normal developmental programs and tissue architecture, and how these processes are studied experimentally.

topics.label: Characteristics, progression, and pathology of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the clinical and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on invasion, metastasis, and the stepwise progression from benign lesions.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standardized naming rules and suffix conventions used to categorize benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue lineages.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the mechanical, systemic, and metastatic pathways through which primary and secondary tumors cause patient illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human tissues and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: They compare tumor incidence and mortality across different human cancer types and examine cancer occurrence throughout diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and methods of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They present the rationale for population-level cancer screening and evaluate diagnostic methods, benefits, and challenges across specific anatomical sites.

topics.label: Conclusion and practical session outlook
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and a preview of upcoming practical sessions.
